2026-07-28

Overview and Recommended AGWRC

AGWRC analysis for USGS 02056900: BLACKWATER RIVER NEAR ROCKY MOUNT, VA. AGWRC analysis for the Blackwater River near Rocky Mount, VA to determine the best 90-day forecast. This gage has 41 recorded baseflow events from 1978-present. The drainage area is 115 mi2. This river empties into Smith Mountain Lake (the other main tributary to the lake is the Roanoke River). The land use is mostly forested or rural with some agriculture and limited development. Iterative AGWRC of 0.97 matched 2002. This gage is very sensitive to start dates due to the frequent ups and downs of flow from precipitation events. For manually selected baseflow events with very low-flows, the lowest trough prediction rather than the 90-day flow allowed for a better comparison between AGWRC values. The AGWRC of 0.97 performed better than the regression AGWRC at the low-flow case studies. The AGWRC of 0.97 appears to be a conservative, reliable estimate for this gage. Recommended AGWRC is a constant value of 0.97

Terminology

Regression AGWRC: the AGWRC calculated by imputing starting flow from manually selected flow event into AGWRC vs Flow Regression

Event AGWRC: the AGWRC from a known baseflow event identified by the workflow

Iterative AGWRC: the manually selected AGWRC that provides the “best fit” for the manually selected baseflow event

Starting flow: the observed flow at the first day of the manually selected baseflow event

MAE: Mean Absolute Error

RMSE: Root Mean Square Error

MAPE: Mean Absolute Percentage Error

Regression Analysis

Image 1. AGWRC vs Flow Regression

The R-squared value is: 0.0013787. This small value suggests that very little of the observed variation in the data can be explained by the regression model.

Second Baseflow Event Investigation

Image 3. Observed and Projected Flows from 2007-06-10

The iterative AGWRC overpredicted the first trough, but predicted the subsequent three troughs well. The iterative and variable AGWRC predictions were effective in surviving the first storm and predicting the first trough, but they greatly underpredicted the remaining flows.

Third Baseflow Event Investigation

Image 4. Observed and Projected Flows from 2002-05-01

Fourth Baseflow Event Investigation

Image 5. Observed and Projected Flows from 1986-05-12
